items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Terminology 63:1
items.html: (To the question) What is the Yesod of Aba that is outside the Yesod of the Nukva? The Mochin of the Nesira that the Nukva receives in the NHY of Ima, which are the Binot and Gevurot of Aba and Ima — here also the NHY of Aba are included in these NHY of Ima. And it is found that at the time that the NHY of Aba clothe in the Yesod of the Nukva, the Yesod of the Nukva is overturned and becomes a male Yesod, like the aspect of Aba. That is, the Yesod of the Nukva is the aspect of short, meaning that there is the aspect of the screen that does not receive the illumination of Hochma but rejects it in the secret of the coupling of striking, and therefore it is called short, which is the opposite of the aspect of long, namely of Hochma, which is called long. As is known. But now, at the time that she receives the Mochin of the Ima of the AB of the Mazalot, it is found that the Yesod of Aba clothes within her short Yesod, and it becomes the aspect of long, like the Yesod of Aba, meaning that she receives there the illumination of Hochma, which is the aspect of Aba. And this illumination of the aspect of long, which she attained in her Yesod at the time that she was in the back of ZA, is called by the name the Yesod of Aba that goes out from outside the Yesod of the Nukva. And this illumination prevails only in the Mochin of the back of the Nukva, when she receives the Mochin from the Mazal, which are the male Gevurot, and she has the Yesod of Aba. However, at the time of her return face to face with ZA, then she no longer receives the Mochin from the NHY of Ima of the AB of the Mazal, but receives the Mochin from the NHY of ZA, which come from the Malchut of Ima that is not included in the Mochin of the Mazal. By her inclusion in the crown of Gevura in the head of ZA, she brings out there the Mochin of Chaya. And then there is in her nothing but female Gevurot, and her Yesod remains short, and the aspect of the Yesod of Aba no longer shines in her Yesod, for now there clothe in her not the NHY of Ima but the NHY of ZA. (Item 210. And in the Ohr Pnimi, in the entry “and this is what the Rav said”).
